execution.progress: build: an inspection round, then paid rounds that persist across interruption; repair and dismantle likewise; inspect takes one round.

details.costs: Study 4 rounds. Every paid round is 1 energy. build: x, y in reach, orientation (open end faces local -y), materials as own items with role rod, binding, thatch or bedding; a measured shortfall is refused at no cost. Round 1 inspects site and items; a failure reserves nothing. Then 9 rounds: legs, ridge and rails, battens twice, covering four times, bedding with final inspection. build naming the shelter resumes. inspect (anyone, site or shelter): 1 round. repair: replacements for defects, a round per metre of binding or 0.05 m3 of covering or bedding. dismantle (empty): 2 rounds. cancel: free. Gathering and travel are extra.
details.effects: Recipe: 20 rigid wood rods (diameter 0.04 m at 0.01 m precision; legs 0.82 m, others 0.9 m long), at least 30 m of strand (vine 3 m, reed 1.8 m a unit), 0.26 m3 of dry thin-stem covering and 0.1 m3 of dry bedding, volumes from mass, water share (dry at most 0.4) and the stem law; dry grass has none. Inputs become one shelter, 1.6 x 0.8 m under a 0.6 m ridge. Complete only after the final inspection. Occupant: one body wholly on the floor that came in by the open end; a second body voids protection. Rated to rain 5 mm/h (index 1 brings 0.033 mm/h) and wind 5 m/s (index 1 read as 5 m/s): rain on the body x(1 - 0.8 x cover), wind chill x(1 - 0.5 x cover x shelter not facing the wind with its open end), dry bedding halves the ground share (0.25) of cooling; air temperature unchanged. Covering holds rain up to its dry mass, leaks through gaps, dries. Strands and covering wear 0.001 a round, 0.002 in rain or wind; below 0.75 gaps open, below 0.5 lashings fail and the frame collapses. Cancel returns unbuilt inputs once; death stops the work and drops them where the person died; built parts stay until dismantled, returned with condition and water. No reward or refund.

packet.access: Omission is not absence. Query abilities, own inventory, knowledge, projects, memory, state or personally observed objects in batches. Ability search/list returns compact catalogue entries; use exact ids for full interface details and applicability. Search results are indexes. Exact queries return one record per offset. All paged records use600-code-unit fragments with zero-based part0..parts-1, consistently in proactive and queried views. Current-scope retained queries are reprojected using these stable pages; original results remain archived. Queries expose no hidden properties, other private records or historical capabilities. Paged records omit their per-record notes: concatenate all parts before parsing; continue with the same exact id. An entry marked inRetrieval is shown with at least the same content under the same id in this input's retrieval. observation.terrain rows are "y:x:cells" strings: each character of cells is the terrain kind of one visible cell, at x, x+1, ... in row y. abilities.baseline entries with id, function and args summarize interfaces you neither used in the last 25 rounds nor need now. args lists the arguments in order: a bare name is a string; otherwise its type with any bounds (number>=lo, integer<=hi, integer lo..hi, and a bare lo..hi is a number range) or its choices a|b; ? marks an optional argument and "" means none. An exact abilities query by id returns the complete contract, including references and string limits of 200 or more code units.
